lessons.title: From diatomic equations of motion to two phonon branches
lessons.summary: Fix the mass normalization and Bloch gauge before examining energy and physical displacements.

sections.title: primitive cell  and two springs
sections.text: The A_l—B_l spring is K₁ and the B_l—A_{l+1} spring is K₂. The primitive-cell length is a and B lies at sa. K, masses and basis positions are independent inputs; changing s does not automatically refit the springs.

sections.title: Eigenvectors are not atomic displacements in a common unit
sections.text: The program solves a two-by-two  Hermitian  matrix in a mass-normalized basis. The Γ acoustic eigenvector is proportional to (√m_A,√m_B); divide by √m to obtain equal-amplitude, in-phase physical displacements of both atoms.

sections.title: Analytic checks of the two branch energies
sections.text: Define t=(K₁+K₂)(1/m_A+1/m_B) and d=4K₁K₂sin²(qa/2)/(m_A m_B). λ_{±} are dynamical-matrix eigenvalues, with energy conversion factor C≈64.654 meV. At Γ the lower branch is rigid translation and the upper branch is relative motion at finite frequency.

sections.title: Why the spectrum has no Γ-point zero-frequency peak
sections.text: The one-phonon formula contains 1/ε and cannot accept a rigid translation directly. The program retains zero-frequency dispersion but excludes modes below an explicit cutoff from the inelastic spectrum. Elastic and quasielastic peaks are not calculated; this does not artificially gap an acoustic mode.
sections.formula: ε<energyCutoff ⇒ exclude from the one-phonon spectrum

lessons.title: For the same  phonon , why does brightness differ between adjacent  reciprocal lattice  zones?
lessons.summary: Distinguish full Q from reduced q and combine projections, basis phases and mass factors in one amplitude.

sections.title: The scattering vector is not the reduced phonon momentum
sections.text: Q is the signed full scan coordinate; Q_{∥}=Qcosθ is its projection onto the chain axis. Reduced q folds into the first  Brillouin zone , while Q_{∥}−q is a  reciprocal lattice  vector. Two measurement points separated by a  reciprocal lattice  vector may have identical  phonon  energies but different intensities.

sections.title: Add amplitudes first, then square
sections.text: Coherent scattering requires adding the two atoms' complex amplitudes first. b is a signed relative scattering amplitude and e is a mass-normalized eigenvector. In the present gauge the creation amplitude must use the complex conjugate of e; omitting phases or conjugation changes extinctions.

sections.title: Calculate extinction by hand in the folded monatomic limit
sections.text: Set the two masses, two springs and two scattering amplitudes equal, with s=1/2. The chosen cell simply doubles a monatomic chain. The folded optical branch is extinct in even reciprocal zones, and the folded acoustic branch in odd zones. Switching the even/odd presets keeps the Hamiltonian fixed and changes only full Q.

sections.title: Treat directional projection and degeneracy separately
sections.text: When Q is perpendicular to the chain, the longitudinal Q·e vanishes and this entire model is dark. Changing the angle also changes reduced q, so cos²θ alone is insufficient. At exact degeneracy, individual-eigenvector intensities are not unique observables; the program reports the sum over the degenerate subspace.

lessons.title: Read temperature and model limits from Stokes / anti-Stokes signals
lessons.summary: Derive detailed balance from Bose factors, distinguishing broadening, cutoffs, material data, and actual lifetimes.

sections.title: Positive energy means the probe loses energy
sections.text: Here Stokes lies at +ε and creates a phonon, while anti-Stokes lies at −ε and annihilates an existing phonon. Their factors are n+1 and n, respectively. Phonons can therefore still be created at zero temperature, but no thermal phonon can be annihilated.

sections.title: Detailed balance tests individual-mode weights
sections.text: This model's real force constants and real scattering weights satisfy  time reversal , so creation and annihilation at the same Q have equal bare weights. The mode-by-mode ratio directly tests Bose statistics; if both processes are dark, their ratio has no experimental meaning.

sections.title: Broadening is not a lifetime, and sampling is not integration
sections.text: Gaussian σ is the standard deviation of the specified resolution; peak area preserves the weight. The program uses erf for finite-window integration and checks ΔE≤σ/2. Once tails cross zero energy or several peaks overlap, the intensity ratio at each sample no longer equals the simple detailed-balance formula.

sections.title: What must be added to move from this model to real files?
sections.text: Long-wavelength fluctuations of an infinite one-dimensional model and the omitted Debye–Waller factor cannot be ignored. This version does not accept real Phonopy scattering input: the existing importer retains complete eigenvectors only for the selected single mode. A realistic calculation needs the primitive cell, Å units, masses, complex eigenvectors for every mode, Q/q matching, scattering weights and suitable thermal-vibration factors. Report the low-energy cutoff and finite Q mesh with the results.

exercises.title: Derive mass factors from the translational zero mode
exercises.prompt: Use the diatomic-chain preset. Check Γ on paper before reading the computed result.

steps.prompt: What actual displacement corresponds to a rigid translation at Γ?
choices: A and B move in phase with equal amplitudes
A and B move with equal amplitudes in opposite phases
The heavier atom must remain stationary
steps.explanation: Equal-amplitude in-phase motion preserves every relative distance and is therefore a zero-restoring-force  acoustic mode .

steps.prompt: What should the ratio of mass-normalized eigenvector components e_A:e_B be?
steps.explanation: To obtain e_A/√m_A=e_B/√m_B, one needs e_A:e_B=√m_A:√m_B.

steps.prompt: At Γ, which quantity is proportional to the optical energy squared?
steps.hint: One eigenvalue of the two-by-two matrix is 0; the other equals its trace.
steps.explanation: λ_{op}=TrD=(K₁+K₂)(1/m_A+1/m_B), multiplied by the square of the energy-conversion constant.

steps.prompt: How should the Γ-point zero-frequency acoustic mode be handled in this inelastic spectrum?
steps.hint: The formula contains 1/ε; this page has no elastic-scattering model.
choices: Exclude it using the explicit low-energy cutoff and report it
Replace it with any finite energy
steps.explanation: Retain the zero-frequency dispersion but exclude it from the one-phonon inelastic formula; broadening or an arbitrary energy cannot be used to invent an elastic peak.

exercises.title: Extinctions interchange in adjacent reciprocal-lattice zones
exercises.prompt: Compare “identical atoms · even  reciprocal lattice  zone” with “adjacent odd  reciprocal lattice  zone”; only full Q changes.

steps.prompt: What happens to reduced q when Q increases by 2π/a?
choices: Return to the same reduced q
steps.explanation: Reduced q is unchanged, so the same Hamiltonian has identical  phonon  energies.

steps.prompt: At s=1/2, what phase does the B basis atom acquire on crossing one reciprocal zone?
steps.explanation: The extra phase is exp(iπ)=−1. A is at the origin and gains no such phase.

steps.prompt: In an odd reciprocal zone, what are the acoustic and optical amplitude factors?
steps.explanation: Acoustic coherent amplitudes cancel while optical amplitudes add; this does not mean  acoustic mode  is absent.

steps.prompt: Why can the bare peak weights of the two presets not be compared using only 0 or 4?
steps.hint: The scattering formula also contains the full-Q projection, masses, and 1/energy.
choices: Retain Q∥², masses, and the 1/ε factor as well
Because the program changed the temperature
Because adjacent zones must have different force constants
steps.explanation: 0/4 is the interference factor. Different full-Q magnitudes also change Q∥², so bright-branch absolute relative weights need not agree.

exercises.title: Derive detailed balance from the energy-gain branch
exercises.prompt: Compare the zero-temperature and 300K presets at fixed model, Q, scattering amplitudes, cutoff, and broadening.

steps.prompt: For T=0, which unbroadened single-mode weights may be nonzero?
steps.hint: Substitute n=0 into W(n+1) and Wn.
steps.explanation: Stokes retains the +1 for zero-point creation; anti-Stokes requires an existing phonon, so its weight is zero.

steps.prompt: If ε=kBT, what is the approximate anti-Stokes/Stokes ratio?
steps.explanation: The ratio is about 0.3679, below 1; for a fixed energy the two weights become closer as temperature rises.

steps.prompt: Can increasing Gaussian broadening σ establish a shorter lifetime?
steps.hint: Here σ is the input energy resolution; no anharmonic self-energy has been calculated.
choices: It directly gives the actual lifetime
No; an independent decay model and resolution analysis are required
The energy integral must increase with σ
steps.explanation: A unit-area Gaussian changes peak width without changing its fully integrated weight. This page does not calculate phonon lifetimes.

cases.title: A mass-contrast prototype for a binary ionic lattice
cases.kind: An ideal model with material context
cases.summary: Use the A/B mass difference to understand acoustic and optical branches, then compare bare weights with visible spectral intensity.
cases.assumption: Only the mass contrast of binary ions is borrowed. The one-dimensional springs and relative b values are teaching parameters, not fits to NaCl's three-dimensional dispersion, polarization, long-range Coulomb interactions, or measured spectrum.

cases.title: The same vibrational mode becomes dark in a different measurement zone
cases.summary: Keep the model and reduced q fixed while changing only the reciprocal zone. Connect basis interference to diffraction extinction, while recognizing that the two use different structure factors.
cases.assumption: The monatomic folded limit, equal b values, and s=1/2 ensure analytic extinction. Inelastic amplitudes also contain eigenvectors, masses, and Q projections, so elastic diffraction intensities cannot simply be copied.

cases.title: From inspecting Phonopy files toward measurable phonon intensities
cases.summary: First check the structure, masses and selected mode in the existing tools, then list the full inputs required for one-phonon intensity. Use the thermal-occupation model to understand an experimental energy-gain branch.
cases.assumption: This version's scattering calculation runs only the diatomic model and does not accept Phonopy files. Frequencies, DOS, or a single-mode animation cannot reconstruct all-mode eigenvectors; the teaching heatmap must not be presented as an imported material's result.
